family.tagline: Four people, one Companion Core, and a house full of books.
family.story: Sally runs a small consultancy from the library, and John writes software in the primary suite. Steve, sixteen, plays upstairs, and Jean, fourteen, studies at her desk. One Companion Core serves all four.

home.lede: Two storeys of brick under a dark shingle roof, with twin chimneys and a white-columned porch at the front. The ground floor is open and lined with books. Behind the house, a pool garden runs down to the lake.

spots.line: A grand piano, shelves of books and the Core on its desk.
A breakfast bar with three stools, where the week's dinners get planned.
Two chesterfield sofas face the TV on its stand.
Jean studies at her own desk, under the lamp.
Steve's room is upstairs, with a desk, a bed and a lamp.

day.line: Sally writes up yesterday's client call before the next one begins.
John starts work at the desk in the primary suite.
The receipts from the shelf are filed before lunch.
Over lunch, the pantry is checked and the shopping list is made.
John pushes the day's branch and closes the laptop.
Jean opens her maths homework as soon as she is in.
Steve drops his bag and starts a session in his room.
Saturday watering by the pool, noted in the plant journal.

members.name: Sally
members.work: consultant, runs her own small practice

companion.name: Juniper
companion.job: Drafts replies to Sally’s clients from the notes she sends it.
companion.limits: Drafts only. Sally reads and sends every message.

profile.bio: Sally runs a small consultancy from the library. She keeps client files, receipts and the week's plan on the Core, and asks Juniper for drafts that she reads before sending.

companion.name: Quill
companion.job: Drafts pull request descriptions from the notes John types to it.
companion.limits: Drafts only. John reads every word before it is used.

profile.bio: John writes software for work from the primary suite. His editor and repositories run on the Core, and Quill drafts his notes on the Core's local model.
Steve plays games that run on the Core, from his room upstairs. His phone photos back up to Immich, and he swaps bin day with Jean.
Jean studies at her own desk: maths in JupyterLab, French with LibreTranslate and notes in Obsidian. Her sources for an essay are saved in Linkwarden.

popup.title: A parcel at the door
popup.body: A parcel waits at the top of the front steps. John carries it through the chess hall and the living room to the library, where Sally clears the desk.

popup.title: Unbox the Companion Core
popup.body: Inside: the Companion Core, a power cable, a quick-start guide and a recovery USB drive. Steve lifts the Core out, and Jean unpacks the guide.

popup.title: Plug it in
popup.body: Steve plugs in the cable. Jean presses the button, and the Core wakes and opens its own Wi-Fi network.

popup.title: Join it from a phone
popup.body: John opens the Wi-Fi settings on his phone and joins the Core’s own network. Then he chooses the home network.

popup.title: Pick the first agent and apps
popup.body: In the Companion Hub store, Sally picks Hermes, and the family adds Nextcloud and Open WebUI. Then they walk away.

beats.capability: an agent that connects to chat apps, email and more from one self-hosted app

popup.title: Juniper says hello
popup.body: Sally messages the agent she named Juniper from the library. Juniper answers from the Core beside her.
popup.note: Messages pass through the chat service you choose.

say.speaker: sally
say.text: Hello, Sally. I am Juniper. What shall we start with?

detail.before: Without an agent of her own, Sally wrote every reply and every reminder herself, one app at a time.
detail.after: Juniper runs in its own sandbox on the Core and answers in the messaging app Sally picked. Messages pass through that chat service.
steps: Pick Hermes in the Companion Hub store
detail.fact: Hermes runs in its own sandbox on your Core and talks to you through the messaging platform you pick.

beats.capability: write a wiki or a set of manuals in books, chapters and pages, with search and history

popup.title: Client notes, in books and pages
popup.body: Sally writes the week's client notes in BookStack on the Core, as books, chapters and pages. Search finds a phrase from any page, and every page keeps its history.

detail.before: Client notes lived as pages in Confluence, and last month’s decisions were found by scrolling.
detail.after: BookStack keeps the notes as books, chapters and pages on the Core. Sally searches a phrase and opens the page's history.
steps: Start a book for the client
Write the week's notes as pages
detail.fact: BookStack is a wiki with a book, chapter and page structure, with search and page history.

beats.capability: scan and file your paperwork; it reads every page, tags it and makes it searchable

popup.title: Receipts and school forms, filed
popup.body: A stack of receipts and school forms leaves the shelf for Paperless-ngx on the Core. Every page is read and searchable, and Sally finds last year’s invoice by one word.

detail.before: Receipts sat in a shoebox, then as photos in Evernote that Sally could only find by remembering the title.
detail.after: Paperless-ngx reads each page on the Core, tags it and files it, so Sally finds an invoice by one word.
detail.fact: Paperless-ngx reads every page, tags it and makes the whole archive searchable.

beats.capability: an agent that connects to chat apps, email and more from one self-hosted app

popup.title: A reply, drafted at the piano
popup.body: From the piano stool, Sally messages Juniper three lines about a moved deadline. Juniper drafts the reply on the Core’s local model, and Sally reads it before sending it herself.
popup.note: Messages pass through the chat service you choose.

say.speaker: sally
say.text: Here is the draft reply. Please check it before it goes.

detail.before: A reply to a client meant opening the mail app, finding the thread and writing it from scratch.
detail.after: Sally texts Juniper three lines. Juniper drafts the reply on the Core's local model, and Sally reads it and sends it herself.
detail.fact: Hermes is an agent built for messaging: it connects to chat apps, email and more from one self-hosted app.

beats.capability: merge, split, compress and convert PDFs on your own Core

popup.title: A heavy scan, made small
popup.body: A client’s scanned report is too big to email. Sally shrinks it with Stirling-PDF on the Core, so the file does not go to a PDF website.

detail.before: A scan too big to email went to a PDF website, or through Adobe Acrobat.
detail.after: Stirling-PDF compresses the scan on the Core. The file does not pass through a PDF website on the way.
detail.fact: Stirling-PDF merges, splits, compresses and converts PDFs on your own Core.

beats.capability: your files, calendar and contacts on your own Core, synced to your devices

popup.title: The contract stays on the Core
popup.body: A client sends the signed contract. Sally files it in Nextcloud, and it sits on the Core, not in a rented drive.

detail.before: A signed contract went into Google Drive, and the file lived on a company's servers.
detail.after: Sally files the contract in Nextcloud. The file sits on the Core and syncs to her devices.
steps: Open it from a phone or a laptop
detail.fact: Nextcloud keeps your files, calendar and contacts on your own Core, synced to your devices.

beats.capability: control and automate your smart home from one place, locally

popup.title: Hall lights and TV, one scene
popup.body: John builds one scene in Home Assistant on the Core. The hall lights and the TV switch together, and the scene runs from the Core with no cloud account.

detail.before: The hall lights lived in the Google Home app, and the television answered to a separate handset.
detail.after: John builds one scene in Home Assistant. It runs on the Core and switches the hall lights and the TV together.
steps: Add the lights and the TV
Run the scene from the hall
detail.fact: Home Assistant controls and automates your smart home from one place, locally, without a cloud account.

beats.capability: stream your own movies, shows and music to every screen in the house

popup.title: Friday’s film, from the collection
popup.body: The family fills the two chesterfields, and Steve picks the film from their own collection. Jellyfin plays it from the Core to the TV.

detail.before: Films from the family collection played through Plex on the television.
detail.after: Jellyfin streams the family's own collection from the Core to the TV, and everyone picks from the same list.
steps: Pick a film from the collection
detail.fact: Jellyfin streams the movies, TV and music you already have to the devices in your home.

beats.capability: track the pantry, shopping lists, recipes, chores and household habits in one place

popup.title: Dinners and one shopping list
popup.body: At the breakfast bar, Sally checks the pantry stock in Grocy on the Core. John adds what is missing to the shopping list, and the list is kept there too.

detail.before: The shopping list lived in AnyList, and nobody could say what was left in the pantry.
detail.after: Grocy tracks pantry stock and shopping lists on the Core, so Sally and John add to and read the same list.
steps: Add what is missing to the list
Tick items off at the shop
detail.fact: Grocy tracks pantry stock, shopping lists, recipes, chores and household habits in one place.

beats.capability: turn habits and chores into a game with levels and quests

popup.title: Bin day earns a level
popup.body: Steve swaps bin day with Jean in Habitica. Each finished chore adds to a level, and the game runs on the Core.

detail.before: Chores were swapped by text message and forgotten by Thursday.
detail.after: Steve and Jean swap bin day in Habitica, and each finished chore adds to a level.
steps: Tick it off when it is done
detail.fact: Habitica turns habits and chores into a game with levels and quests.

beats.capability: write code in VS Code in your browser, with the editor and your files on your Core

popup.title: The editor is already there
popup.body: John opens his laptop, and the editor is waiting. Code Server runs on the Core, so his files sit at home, not in a cloud editor.

detail.before: John coded in Cursor on his laptop, with the project folder on that one machine.
detail.after: Code Server gives John the same kind of editor in a browser tab. The editor and his files are on the Core.
steps: Open the editor in a browser
detail.fact: Code Server runs VS Code in your browser, with the editor and your files on your Core.

beats.capability: host your own git repositories, issues and pull requests on your Core

popup.title: The day’s branch goes home
popup.body: John pushes the day’s branch to Forgejo from the laptop on his desk. The repository sits in the house, on the Core, with its issues and pull requests beside it.

detail.before: The day's branch went to GitHub, with the issues and pull requests kept there.
detail.after: Forgejo hosts the repository on the Core, with its issues and pull requests beside it.
steps: Open a pull request in Forgejo
detail.fact: Forgejo hosts your own Git repositories, issues and pull requests on your Core.

beats.capability: an agent that connects to chat apps, email and more from one self-hosted app

popup.title: Quill drafts the pull request
popup.body: From the loveseat, John types his notes to Quill in his browser. Quill drafts the description on the Core’s local model, and John reads it before pasting it into Forgejo.

say.speaker: john
say.text: Here is the description. Please read it before you paste it.

detail.before: Describing a change meant writing the pull request text by hand after a long day.
detail.after: Quill drafts the description on the Core's local model. John reads it, edits it and pastes it into Forgejo himself.
detail.fact: Hermes is an agent built for messaging: it connects to chat apps, email and more from one self-hosted app.

beats.capability: run Steam on your Core and play it in a browser on a screen in the house

popup.title: The game runs a floor below
popup.body: Steve opens his Steam library in a browser in his room. Steam Headless runs his session a floor below, on the Core, not on a cloud gaming service.

detail.before: A cloud gaming service such as GeForce Now runs the session in a data centre and streams it to the player.
detail.after: Steam Headless runs the session on the Core, and Steve plays it in a browser in his room.
steps: Open the library in the browser
detail.fact: Steam Headless runs Steam on your Core and plays it in a browser on a screen in the house.

beats.capability: run Steam on your Core and play it in a browser on a screen in the house

popup.title: Where the session runs
popup.body: A cloud gaming service would run the session on its servers. Here it runs on the Core, in the house. Valve keeps the account and the library.

detail.before: GeForce Now runs the game on its own servers, so the session lives there.
detail.after: On the Core the session runs in the house. Valve still keeps the account and the library.
steps: Start the session on the Core
detail.fact: Steam needs a Valve account to sign in. The game library and the purchases are Valve's, and the Core runs the session.

beats.capability: back up, search and organise your family photos and videos

popup.title: Steve’s photos land on the Core
popup.body: A summer of photos from Steve’s phone backs up to Immich on the Core, not to a photo cloud. The first start takes a while, because Immich sorts the pictures.

detail.before: Steve's phone photos backed up to Google Photos and sat in a company's cloud.
detail.after: Immich backs them up to the Core instead. It sorts the pictures, so the first start takes a while.
steps: Install Immich from the Companion Hub store
detail.fact: Immich backs up, organises and searches your family photos and videos on your own Core.

beats.capability: write and run notebooks, code and data in a browser, on your Core

popup.title: Maths homework, worked in code
popup.body: Jean works her maths homework in a JupyterLab notebook on the Core. She tries each problem in code, then checks it against her own answer.

detail.before: A stuck homework question went to a search engine or a hosted chat tool.
detail.after: Jean runs her notebook in JupyterLab on the Core and checks each answer against her own working.
steps: Open the notebook in the browser
detail.fact: JupyterLab writes and runs notebooks, code and data in a browser, on your Core.

beats.capability: save web pages with a screenshot and PDF so they survive link rot

popup.title: Pages saved for the essay
popup.body: For her history essay, Jean saves each source page in Linkwarden. It keeps a screenshot and a PDF on the Core, so the page survives if the link dies.

detail.before: Sources for an essay were saved as bookmarks in Raindrop.io, and the page itself stayed out on the web.
detail.after: Linkwarden saves each page with a screenshot and a PDF on the Core, so Jean can still read it if the link dies.
detail.fact: Linkwarden saves web pages with a screenshot and PDF so they survive link rot.

beats.capability: translate text and documents on your own Core

popup.title: French first, then checked
popup.body: Jean writes her French paragraph herself, then checks it in LibreTranslate. Its language models were downloaded once, and the Core does the translating, not a translation website.

detail.before: Checking a French paragraph meant pasting it into Google Translate.
detail.after: LibreTranslate runs on the Core with language models the family downloaded once. Jean pastes her paragraph there instead.
steps: Compare it with her own version
detail.fact: LibreTranslate translates text and documents on your own Core.

beats.capability: the Obsidian note app in your browser; notes stay as local Markdown files

popup.title: Study notes as plain files
popup.body: Cross-legged on her bed, Jean types up the day’s study notes in Obsidian. It runs in a browser session, and the notes are plain Markdown files on the Core.

detail.before: Study notes lived as pages inside Notion.
detail.after: Obsidian runs in a browser session on the Core. The notes are plain Markdown files that any text editor can open.
steps: Open the vault in the browser
detail.fact: Obsidian is a note app in your browser. Your notes stay as local Markdown files.

beats.capability: track your plants, watering and care history across rooms and beds, with photos and a garden journal

popup.title: Saturday watering, noted in the garden
popup.body: On Saturday, Jean records the watering of the garden beds by the pool in HortusFox. The plant journal sits on the Core.

detail.before: Watering was remembered, or forgotten, with no record of which bed got what.
detail.after: Jean logs each watering in HortusFox. The journal of beds, dates and photos sits on the Core.
detail.fact: HortusFox tracks your plants, watering and care history across rooms and beds, with photos and a garden journal.

popup.title: A house of books, one Core
popup.body: Planner, files, code, games and homework run on one Companion Core, among the library’s books.

closing.body: Your calendar, contracts, code and homework can sit on a Companion Core at home. Browse the Companion Hub store and pick your first apps.

notes: suite-code uses code-server, which has no QA screenshot: the app-qa-screenshot review item has an owner entry in content/story/reviewed.json (slug brennan, at suite-code).
Told in the v3 shape: sixteen pair beats name a service from content/story/services.json; the four pair-less beats are two Hermes drafts, JupyterLab and HortusFox.
Jean is fourteen and has no chat model in her own beats (age rule 16); Open WebUI is only named in the first-install list, which has no member.
Steam Headless: Valve account named, no frame rate, no title, home network only. Steve is never shown asleep.
